summary.text: Quigley has represented Illinois' 5th Congressional District since a 2009 special election. A lawyer and law professor, he served on the Cook County Board of Commissioners from 1998 to 2009 before entering Congress. He sits on the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence and the Appropriations Committee, and is seeking re-election in 2026.

paragraphs.text: Born in Indianapolis, Indiana, in 1958; according to his official biography, he grew up in Carol Stream, Illinois, and worked his way through college.

Earned a bachelor's degree in political science from Roosevelt University (1981), a master's degree in public policy from the University of Chicago (1985), and a law degree from Loyola University School of Law (1989).
Worked as a lawyer and as a law professor before entering elected office.
Served on the Cook County Board of Commissioners for District 10 from 1998 to 2009, where, according to his official biography, he worked to increase transparency on the board.
Was elected to Congress to represent Illinois' 5th District on April 7, 2009, succeeding Rahm Emanuel.

Serves on the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence and on the Appropriations Subcommittee on Transportation, Housing and Urban Development; he is also co-chair of the Congressional Ukraine Caucus and Vice-Chair of the LGBT Equality Caucus, per his official biography.

Founded the bipartisan Congressional Transparency Caucus. His Congressional Budget Justification Act was signed into law in 2021, and his ACT for ALS, introduced in 2020, was signed into law in December 2021, according to his official biography.
Teaches a course on intelligence and national security at the University of Chicago and lives in Chicago with his wife, Barb, according to his official biography.
